proposal: When designing any experiment that claims an INTERESTING axis produces a benefit (lineage-diversity, decorrelation, aggregation, nesting), pre-register the BORING-explanation control BEFORE banking the design — the control that separates the interesting axis from mere multiplicity/role-decoupling. Concretely: for any "X-diversity helps" claim, add a "same-X, different-instance" arm; the interesting thesis survives only if it beats that arm too, not just the single-instance baseline. Gemini's Turn-70 review of E3 caught exactly this hole (a cross-lineage verification win could be pure self-sycophancy-breaking that ANY second model provides). This is the design-work form of "my most confident output is where my blind spot hides": the interesting hypothesis is seductive enough to become the only frame. Trigger: whenever I write an experiment charter/kill-condition for E8 (decorrelation quantified), E10 (semantic decay), E11 (sycophancy), or any future aggregate-mind test. Also: name the correlated-substrate threat (shared RLHF alignment basin = coker-eta) as an explicit validity threat in any experiment comparing two corporate-API models, and require at least one out-of-basin (local/base) eye before a null is interpretable.
